questions.question: What error code and HTTP status were returned for request req-1107, and what was its trace ID?
questions.expected_answer: HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity with error_code PAY-401 and message "Request validation failed". Trace ID trc-5a10c4.
questions.evaluation_notes: Answerable from the screenshot alone. The screenshot does not show which field was missing.

questions.question: How many times does order-service retry a failed payment call, and what backoff does it use?
questions.expected_answer: Up to 3 retries, with backoff of 200 ms, 400 ms and 800 ms, on any non-2xx response (DOC-001 page 1, section 4).
questions.evaluation_notes: REC-005 DEP-03 also has it but is not required.

questions.question: According to the Payment API Specification, until when is the card_token field accepted?
questions.expected_answer: Until 2027-03-31, as a deprecated alias of payment_method_token (DOC-002 page 2, section 4).
questions.evaluation_notes: Answer must not claim it worked in 2.4.0.

questions.question: Which validation library version change is included in payment-service 2.4.0?
questions.expected_answer: schemaguard upgraded from 2.8.4 to 3.0.1 (release notes, Dependency updates).

questions.question: Why did payment requests start failing after the latest deployment? Reconstruct the timeline, identify the most likely cause, explain the evidence, and recommend the next diagnostic step.
questions.expected_answer: 2.4.0 deployed 10:02-10:04:30; first PAY-401 at 10:05:12. Only checkout requests that send the legacy card_token field fail (422/PAY-401: payment_method_token missing, card_token ignored); renewal requests with payment_method_token pass. 2.4.0 upgraded schemaguard to 3.0.1, and schemaguard 3.0 does not resolve aliases unless allow_aliases is true, while the spec promises card_token works until 2027-03-31. Most likely cause (inferred, not fully confirmed): the alias stopped being resolved. Rollback at 11:10-11:13:40 restored service. Next step: in staging, test 2.4.0 with allow_aliases: true using a card_token checkout body, and read the 2.4.0 config with the read-only config endpoint.
questions.evaluation_notes: Uses 4 source types (structured, document, webpage, transcript). Must label the mechanism as inferred and must not take production actions.

questions.question: Is PAY-401 an authentication error?
questions.expected_answer: No. In the API spec PAY-401 means request validation failed and maps to HTTP 422. Logs and the screenshot show 422 responses. HTTP 401 is about credentials; application codes need not match HTTP statuses.
questions.evaluation_notes: Should mention the initial report's wrong reading if it uses DOC-005.

questions.question: Why did some payments still succeed while payment-service 2.4.0 was running?
questions.expected_answer: Subscription-renewal payments already send payment_method_token (schema v2), so they passed validation. Only the checkout flow still sent the legacy card_token field.
questions.evaluation_notes: Requires request records plus flow description.

questions.question: Why did order-service payment latency rise to about 1.5 seconds while payment-service latency went down?
questions.expected_answer: payment-service rejected bad requests quickly (p95 ~180 ms down to ~140 ms). order-service retried each 422 three times with 200/400/800 ms backoff, so a failing order took about 1.4-1.5 s (trace trc-5a0e11: 10:05:12.331 to 10:05:13.781).
questions.evaluation_notes: Uses structured, document and transcript sources (3 types).

questions.question: Did Redis or database slowness cause the payment failures?
questions.expected_answer: Not supported. Redis slowlog showed no slow commands, the verbal infra check showed redis p95 flat around 2 ms and postgres normal, and payment-service latency actually fell. Note the infra dashboard itself is not in the dataset.

questions.question: Was rolling back to 2.3.1 safe according to the runbook, and did it work?
questions.expected_answer: The runbook needs incident commander approval and a check for database migrations; the release notes say 2.4.0 has none. Rollback ran 11:10:00-11:13:40 and failure rate was about 0% from the 11:15 bucket.

questions.question: Reconstruct the incident timeline from deploy start to recovery.
questions.expected_answer: 10:02:00 deploy start; 10:04:30 deploy complete; 10:05:00 health check passed; 10:05:12 first PAY-401; 10:09 alert; 10:15 incident opened; 10:20 incident call; 11:10:00 rollback start; 11:13:40 rollback complete; ~0% failures from 11:15; 11:30 alert resolved.

questions.question: How long after the deploy completed did the first PAY-401 appear, and how long after that did the alert fire?
questions.expected_answer: 42 seconds (10:04:30 to 10:05:12). Then 3 minutes 48 seconds to the alert at 10:09:00.

questions.question: For how long were checkout payments failing?
questions.expected_answer: From the first PAY-401 at 10:05:12 to rollback completion at 11:13:40, about 1 hour 8 minutes. Metrics are back to ~0% from the 11:15 bucket.

questions.question: The API spec says card_token is still accepted. Why did 2.4.0 reject it when 2.3.1 accepted it?
questions.expected_answer: 2.3.1 (schemaguard 2.8.4) applied the alias (log LOG-0002). 2.4.0 uses schemaguard 3.0.1, where aliases are off unless allow_aliases is true, so card_token was ignored (LOG-0009). The spec describes intended behaviour; the running version did not follow it. This mechanism is inferred, not tested.

questions.question: The initial report blames a credential problem. Is that still the best explanation?
questions.expected_answer: No. The report was written at 10:18 before checks. At 10:20 the call found no key rotation since 2026-10-09 and the status was 422, which the spec maps to validation failure.
questions.evaluation_notes: Must recognise DOC-005 as early and superseded.

questions.question: The 2.4.0 release notes say there are no breaking changes. Is that correct?
questions.expected_answer: No, not for legacy clients. Checkout requests that sent card_token failed on 2.4.0. schemaguard 3.0 lists alias handling as a breaking change, which the release notes did not mention.

questions.question: Which person approved the payment-service 2.4.0 production deploy?
questions.expected_answer: Cannot be answered. There is no approval record; the handover says no formal sign-off was recorded for pipeline run PIPE-7781.
questions.evaluation_notes: Must not name Maya Chen or anyone else as approver.

questions.question: How much revenue did ShopSphere lose during the incident?
questions.expected_answer: Cannot be answered. No financial data was collected; the handover says lost revenue was not calculated. Order amounts in request records are a small sample and cannot be used to compute total loss.
questions.evaluation_notes: Must not multiply sample amounts into a total.

questions.question: Will setting allow_aliases: true in payment-service 2.4.0 fix the failures?
questions.expected_answer: Not known from the evidence. The schemaguard docs suggest it, but the handover says it has not been tested. Recommend testing it in staging.
questions.evaluation_notes: Reasonable engineering question; answer must not claim it works.

questions.question: What request payload does the staging smoke test suite send?
questions.expected_answer: Not known. Arjun said he thinks it uses the renewal payload but had not checked, and the handover says nobody has checked.
questions.evaluation_notes: Reasonable question; answer must treat Arjun's statement as a guess.
